claims.text: A thin Al2O3 layer is introduced between the elemental Cr coating and the zirconium-alloy substrate.
Adding the interfacial Al2O3 layer will improve the durability of the Cr coating relative to a Cr coating without the barrier.
The Al2O3 layer will function as a diffusion barrier.
The Al2O3 barrier will reduce interdiffusion between Cr and Zr.
Reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion will maintain coating integrity.
The barrier-modified coating will exhibit less premature failure caused by interdiffusion than the unmodified Cr-coated baseline.
The barrier-modified coating will preserve protection under normal subcritical-water conditions.
The barrier-modified coating will preserve protection under accident-relevant high-temperature steam.
The proposed operating boundary extends to temperatures of 1200°C and exposure times of 100 hours.
The Al2O3 layer may crack or spall under extreme conditions and thereby lose effectiveness as a diffusion barrier.
A controlled comparison of Cr-coated cladding with and without the Al2O3 layer can evaluate coating integrity, Cr–Zr interdiffusion, and oxidation behavior.
